review_scope: parity-expression-bindings bounded source and semantics review

declarations.parity_review: Reviewed loads remote CLI models from the selected node and keeps Jait on the gateway. Original body, setup, imports, lifecycle and every assertion operand match the bounded AST audit. The TypeScript printer and parser normalize code by syntax tokens, preserving string, template and RegExp literal content and automatic semicolon insertion. Nine full source-binding mutations and nine token controls reject changed operands, literal whitespace and changed ASI behavior while accepting layout-only whitespace. The AST audit requires the original expect.stringMatching call for nested text-pattern rules and excludes ordinary RegExp equality; four pattern controls verify that distinction. The Vitest revival applies real asymmetric string matchers in equality and call-argument contexts, with plain RegExp values retained for toMatch/toThrow. Thirty-four raw-domain controls include nested and hybrid regex bounds, checked captured operand indices, custom serialization rejection and marker spoofing. All 42 observations and 42 opposing counterexamples agree. One zero-count optional assertion belongs to the statically unreachable expectThreadTurnMessage helper; its original body remains present, the bounded call-graph proof records its lack of reachable calls, and the existing unused-helper regression controls passed again. This does not claim that helper was exercised. The live coverage audit separately reports concurrent changes in agent-loop.ts and agent-loop-compaction.test.ts; these declarations remain bound to the recorded frozen runtime and do not establish parity for those newer runtime edits. Every observation and an opposing counterexample agree between real Vitest and Rust. Bindings, per-site counts and source hashes: .jait/artifacts/parity-exceptions/source-checkpoint/.jait/artifacts/parity-expression-bindings/combined-selected.json. Full translated, internal, managed, formatting and Clippy validation passed on the unchanged exception checkpoint. Candidate originals, peers, comparator and transport hashes also match the live checkout. The initial full report exposed a queue timing failure (expected 409, actual 200); that report and three isolated passing unmodified Vitest runs are retained in .jait/artifacts/parity-exceptions/queue-timing-observation.json. No queue assertion or application behavior was changed, and the subsequent complete full run passed. This establishes preservation of the exercised reference-test domains, not native runtime parity or absence of reference-test flakes.
